title: Reduce streaming token latency: token loop, flush cadence, backpressure, and kernel scheduling
author: Ava Patel
description: Motivation: Customers reported tail and p50 latency regressions for streaming generation under mixed workloads. Investigation pointed to three interacting areas: the token emission loop flush cadence, naive backpressure propagation across batching boundaries, and suboptimal kernel scheduling that causes short-lived kernel launches for small microbatches. This PR introduces a coordinated set of runtime changes to reduce end-to-end streaming token latency across typical PLG workloads. Summary of changes: 1) Token loop: rework the streaming token emission loop to avoid per-token syscall/flushs and amortize serialization by emitting tokens in small bounded micro-bursts (configurable flush_cadence_ms). 2) Flush cadence: introduce a hysteresis-backed flush scheduler that batches emitted tokens up to a short time window (default 8ms) or size cap, whichever comes first, reducing syscall overhead while keeping interactive latency. 3) Backpressure propagation: add an explicit lightweight backpressure token to slow producers when downstream socket buffers are saturated; this avoids queue pile-up and provides reactive throttling compatible with continuous batching. 4) Kernel scheduling: coalesce tiny microbatches at the scheduling layer and prefer running a single slightly larger launch rather than many sub-10-token launches; integrate with the runtime kernel cost heuristic to pick fused kernels for short-seq inference. 5) KV cache / batching interaction: modify KV cache hot-path to expose fast-path reads without mutex contention and to allow early KV population for coalesced microbatches. Results: internal bench runs (benchmark-lab; 4x A10g mixed seq workloads) show median per-token latency improvement from 12.4ms -> 7.1ms (~43% reduction) and p95 from 38ms -> 18ms. Under high-concurrency streaming (200 rps), observed fewer socket stalls and 2.6x reduction in incidents of multi-token flush gaps >50ms. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on runtime flag streaming_latency_opt_v1; gradual rollout to 10% canaries with perf dashboards and auto rollback on regression. Backwards compatibility: no API change; flush cadence is configurable via runtime config and defaults tuned conservatively. Checklist: - [x] Microbenchmarks (unit + perf harness) - [x] End-to-end streaming e2e tests - [x] Compatibility with dedicated/private infra - [x] Feature flag + rollout plan - [x] Release notes entry - [x] Docs snippet for new runtime config knobs Risks & mitigations: slight increase in batching delay (configurable); mitigated by small default window and ability to set per-route SLOs. Kernel scheduling heuristics were validated across a range of model sizes; a fallback to previous scheduler is available via a runtime flag. Related: ENG-4321, ENG-4330, see internal notes and benchmark runs linked in the ticket.

review_conversation: Diego Ramos (2026-02-16): Great work on the flush scheduler. Two questions: 1) How did you pick 8ms default? 2) Can we expose per-route override?

Ava Patel (2026-02-16): 8ms came from the pareto curve in benchmark-lab across our PLG traces; it's the knee where p50 improves with minimal p99 regression. Per-route override is added as runtime_config.route.flush_cadence_ms (see runtime/config/runtime_config.rs).
Priya Menon (2026-02-18): The kernel heuristic change worries me for very short sequences on older GPUs. Is there a safe rollback?

Ava Patel (2026-02-18): Added fallback flag kernel_scheduler.use_coalesce (false by default on release branches). We also log the scheduling decision to tracing so we can detect bad decisions in the canary window.
Liu Chen (2026-02-20): Observed a rare panic in the backpressure path under shutdown in integ test. Can you add a guard?
Ava Patel (2026-02-21): Fixed the race (see commit h9c1e5f) and added a unit test that simulates abrupt stream termination.
Diego Ramos (2026-02-24): Perf dashboards look solid for canaries. Approved.
Priya Menon (2026-02-25): LGTM after a small nits patch. Approved.
release_notes:
- Reduced streaming per-token latency (~43% p50 improvement) by reworking token loop, flush cadence, backpressure handling, and kernel scheduling.
- New runtime knobs: runtime_config.stream.flush_cadence_ms, runtime_config.kernel_scheduler.coalesce_microbatches.
- Default conservative rollout behind feature flag streaming_latency_opt_v1.
